title: Probability tree for Bayes' theorem
back: Multiply along a path. $P(D)$ is the sum of the paths ending in $D$, here $0.0345$. $P(B\mid D)$ = path through $B$ ÷ $P(D)$.

title: Conditional probability
legend: F = the event known to have occurred, P(F) ≠ 0
back: Given goes down. With equally likely outcomes: $\dfrac{n(E\cap F)}{n(F)}$.

title: Multiplication theorem
back: "And" means multiply, with the second probability taken after the first has happened (without replacement: the numbers change).

title: Independent events
back: Then $E'$ and $F'$ are independent too. To test independence, compute both sides separately and compare.

title: At least one (independent events)
back: "The problem is solved" = at least one solves it. Exactly one: $P(A)P(B')+P(A')P(B)$.

title: Mutually exclusive is not independent
back: Two events with non-zero probabilities cannot be both. A favourite assertion–reason pair.

title: Theorem of total probability
legend: E_j = each cause: a partition of the sample space
back: For each route: (chance of the route) × (chance of the event on that route). Then add.

title: Bayes' theorem
legend: A = the event that has been observed
back: Define the events in words and list the probabilities first: those two lines carry marks.

title: Probability distribution
back: Use "total = 1" to find an unknown $k$; reject a value that makes any probability negative.

title: Mean of a random variable
back: Multiply each value by its probability and add. Two cards, number of aces: mean $=\dfrac{2}{13}$.
